record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the tenth International conference on fuzzy set theory and applications (FSTA 2010, Liptovsky Jan, Slovakia)
record.original_question: Provide an alternative characterization of all quasi-triangular norms. Here a track is a set {(f(t),g(t)): t in [0,1]} where f and g are nondecreasing continuous surjections from [0,1] to [0,1], and a binary operation U on [0,1] is a quasi-triangular norm if for every track B there exists a triangular norm T_B that agrees with U on B.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ be a triangular norm, i.e. a binary operation on $[0,1]$ that is commutative, associative, nondecreasing in each argument, and satisfies $T(1,x)=x$ for all $x\in[0,1]$. Define a track to be a subset of $[0,1]^2$ of the form
$$B_{f,g}=\{(f(t),g(t)):t\in[0,1]\},$$
where $f,g:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ are nondecreasing continuous surjections. A binary operation $U:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ is called a quasi-triangular norm if for every track $B$ there exists a triangular norm $T_B$ such that $U(x,y)=T_B(x,y)$ for all $(x,y)\in B$.

Provide an alternative (intrinsic, non-track-based) characterization of the class of all quasi-triangular norms on $[0,1]$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not reveal a published alternative characterization of quasi-triangular norms in the sense described (tracks of pairs of nondecreasing continuous surjections from [0,1]). Surveys on construction methods for triangular norms and related FSTA 2010 problem lists do not appear to record a resolution; current status is unclear.

status_evidence.title: How to construct left-continuous triangular norms—state of the art
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of construction methods for (left-continuous) t-norms; no characterization of quasi-triangular norms via tracks is given.
status_evidence.claim: No alternative characterization of quasi-triangular norms recorded in standard t-norm surveys.

status_evidence.title: Designing and learning of adjustable quasi-triangular norms
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces a parameterized family of quasi-triangular norms for neuro-fuzzy applications, not addressing the track-based characterization problem.
status_evidence.claim: Existing 'quasi-triangular norm' literature targets a different (parametric) notion.
